evidence: Workbook row 25 and skill quality-checks.md section 25 ('every prompt opens http://localhost:3000 and directs the judge to the Playwright MCP tool; defect: any prompt that could be satisfied by reading source, memory, or a first paint'). All five frozen prompts open with the required sentence at prompt.md:1: constraints 'Evaluate the live Colderwater playground at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP. Use only rendered browser behavior and the live DOM.'; render '... using Playwright MCP. Use only rendered browser behavior.'; functional, polish and visual '... using Playwright MCP.' Each of the five judge.toml files wires the playwright stdio MCP server (playwright-mcp --headless --isolated), and tests/Dockerfile installs @playwright/mcp with chromium. Source scoring is excluded: constraints prompt.md:5 'decide it from the listed DOM facts only, not from file names, bundled library names or how the code looks'; functional prompt.md:22 'do not read implementation files to infer success'; polish prompt.md:19 'do not read implementation files'; visual prompt.md:20 'Do not read implementation files and do not infer behavior from styling'. Memory/inherited scoring is excluded: functional prompt.md:11 and polish prompt.md:11 'A criterion passes only on evidence you gathered yourself in this session for that criterion. If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass.'; visual prompt.md:13 'Score from screenshots and the rendered page you observed yourself in this session'. First-paint scoring is excluded: the render gate criterion requires clicking into the editor, typing a word with real keys, seeing it, and reloading (gates/render/judge.toml:23) and the prompt says 'a static shell whose editor cannot be typed into fails'; functional, polish and visual each carry a global browser gate requiring 'that text typed into the code editor appears in it' (prompt.md:5); visual prompt.md:14 requires entering a ten-line draft, pressing Run, clicking into the code, a double-click selection and screenshots before scoring; every one of the 43 functional, 6 polish and 2 constraints criteria prescribes real key/mouse interaction and a readback. Weak-app probe: a static pretty shell that never accepts typing fails the render gate and the in-prompt gates, so it cannot earn first-paint credit; a source-only reading cannot satisfy any criterion because each demands observed state after interaction. Conforming-alternative probe: a canvas-drawn editor is still gradable in-browser (app_context.md:29 'read colours and text from screenshots instead of computed styles'). Supporting run evidence on an earlier candidate (not these bytes): hosted judge reasonings quote browser actions, e.g. gates 'Typed QUARTZFOX-xyzzy into the code area with real key presses (page.keyboard after a real click ...). Read-only DOM inspection showed ...' and functional 'Home+Backspace produced exactly [alpha onebeta two] on one line, and one Ctrl+Z restored ...'. Notes (not defects for this row): (1) the render and constraints gate prompts do not carry an explicit 'do not read implementation files' sentence like the three scored prompts; they rely on 'Use only rendered browser behavior' / 'the live DOM', which is equivalent in effect and matches the template wording. (2) No configured judge run exists for these exact bytes; the only prompt change since the hosted run is the added 'checker, not a fixer' paragraph, which tightens rather than loosens browser-only grading, and this row is a prompt-text property, so the missing run is recorded as NOT EXERCISED rather than as a risk for this row.
